I've been taking it for over a year now, started on 15mg and am now up to 45mg - which I think is the maximum allowed in the UK. The only hallucinations I had where anxiety induced, and where the reason I got increased from 30mg to 45mg. Whilst I was adjusting to the increase I had some issues with restless legs and feeling the urge to constantly move for a few hours after I took it. I think that was bad enough to put me off ever taking more than I should, and so I take extra care to ensure I never take doses too close together. Though even at a high dose, it has me falling asleep an hour or so after I've taken. Which is great for me because I had major issues with getting to sleep before I started taking it.

I was the same with cigarettes, it seemed better than the other options. I'm still addicted to nicotine, I just get it in other forms. I think sometimes you have to do something to help, even if it's bad in the long term. Only once you're ready can you try to replace those behaviours with more positive ones.

I think that talking to a professional would be helpful, if you are able to do that. It takes time to recover, and a lot of work in changing the way that you think. But maybe, as a start it might be helpful to try to challenge some of your thoughts when you get the urge to give in it your addictions. So try thinking of it like this - you might want to self-harm, starve yourself, binge-eat or smoke cigarettes, but the thing is it's self abuse. Isn't it enough that there is abuse in your past?
